summary: Records finished Reality Scan runs into the Yard's run records, one run at a time, and prints the totals.
purpose: Makes the Reality Scan results appear in the Yard for all runs that are complete.
why: Likely reason: earlier scan runs were not recorded in the Yard, so this fills them in. The header says the recording replaces each run's records in one transaction.
how: Loads every Reality Scan run with status succeeded. Keeps only the one given on the command line, if any. For each run, records it in the Yard, adds its counts into running totals, and counts the runs. Prints the number of runs and totals, then exits.
inputs: An optional run ID as the first command argument. The realityScanRuns table in the database, and the recording function from the Reality Scan yardRecords module.
outputs: Yard run records for each selected scan run, and one console line with the run count and totals by kind.
risks: Writes to the database. The header says records are replaced for each run, so re-running replaces existing records for that run. If one run fails, the loop stops.
debug: If the total shows zero runs, check that the run has status succeeded in realityScanRuns. If it stops partway, rerun with that run's ID. The replacement behaviour is in the imported function, so check that file if records look wrong.
